angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 377,069 km at 182.33 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4844 +/- 0.0326 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 182.33 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.542 +/- 0.049 solar radii from Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-43 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract): 377,069 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.571 +/- 0.111 solar masses from Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-43 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3840.6 +/- 98.8 K from Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-43 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-43 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-43.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.727, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-43 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.21241, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
